# Quality Gates — Web / Frontend

_Applies when: finishing any React / frontend change — the web overlay on `30-quality.md`._

Web-only additions to the neutral DoD in `30-quality.md` — this never restates it. The generic green
gate, the `verify` step, and the Definition of Done live there; only the web specifics are below.

## Full green gate — web specifics

- `lint` **with FSD boundary checks** (`--max-warnings=0`), layered on the generic lint / typecheck /
  full-suite. Wire it as a Husky pre-commit hook + lint-staged (`eslint --fix` + Prettier) — **and wire
  a `pre-merge-commit` hook that spells out what it runs**: a conflict-free `git merge` commits itself
  and fires that hook in place of `pre-commit`, while husky's shim exits 0 without a word when no user
  file sits next to it (measured, git 2.53.0 + husky 9.1.7), so incoming foreign work passes the gate
  with no output at all.
  Sourcing `pre-commit` from it is the wrong shortcut — where `skill:setup-changelog`'s opt-in hook is
  in place, that runs a version bump into a live merge. After merging foreign work, run the full
  `lint` over the merged tree and quote the **scanned file count**.
- **Boundary lint fails open**: `eslint-plugin-boundaries` silently drops imports it cannot resolve —
  green at severity `error`. Per fail-loud, trust the file count it reports, never its exit code. Keep
  the canary OUT of any test-glob location where the rule is off (`**/__tests__/**` overrides commonly
  disable boundaries): the fixture lives in the slice root, only the test sits under `__tests__/`.
  The canary must use an **aliased** import (a relative one errors even with a dead resolver — a false
  green) and must assert the **exact rule id** in the report: that one assertion covers all three ways
  the gate goes quiet — unresolvable import, rule silenced by missing options, rule gone at a major
  (`10-fsd`).
- `build` succeeds (Turbo); offline single-file tools must stay `file://`-compatible (no external CDN,
  inline SVG/CSS). Code duplication < 5% (jscpd; minTokens 50, minLines 5). No hardcoded values —
  config lives in `shared/config/`.
- **React Doctor** clean on the changed scope — zero new `error`-severity findings (`react-doctor`
  pinned to an exact version; `--scope changed --blocking error --no-score --no-supply-chain`).
  Evidence is the `--json` findings + scanned-file count, never the exit code (fail-open paths exist)
  and never the remote score. Advisory until the modified-MIT AI-training clause is legally cleared.
  Mechanics + FP-tuning live in `skill:react-doctor`.

## UI work — verify visually (mandatory)

- "Green tests" is not done. Open the UI in a browser (claude-in-chrome / Playwright) and **look at
  it**; capture screenshots. A build that passes but looks flat or broken is a defect, not a pass —
  aim high-end and design-led (design / impeccable / frontend-design skills).
- **A run against intercepted routes proves the surface, not the system — and a service worker answers
  the network before either.** Where `route(…).fulfill(…)`, a faked auth state or an in-memory stub
  replies, the claim is only "at THIS payload the UI renders so": no field name, status code or server
  default is refuted. An active service worker widens that silently — Playwright does not see the
  requests it intercepts, so block workers where the harness can and the worker is not itself under
  test (`serviceWorkers: 'block'` on the context, `--block-service-workers` on the Playwright MCP
  server; both stop NEW registrations only, a profile that already holds a worker keeps it) — and the
  same worker keeps serving the OLD precached bundle after a rebuild, so a missing element is a false
  negative, not a missing feature. Therefore: **measure** the interception reach as a number instead of
  asserting it (registered rules vs. requests that reached the real service — a catch-all over the
  whole origin makes it zero, not small), read the loaded build's identity BEFORE asserting (the hashed
  asset name in the served HTML; an injected version string only where the app provides one), detect
  the worker with `navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations()`/`.controller` instead of guessing "is
  this a PWA", and drive at least one path through the real edge — create once, save once, load once
  against the running service (`skill:verify`).
- Gotchas: `file://` is blocked by the browser tool (serve via `http.server`); rAF freezes in hidden
  tabs; load demo data so rich states are visible; rebuild before re-testing to avoid a stale bundle.
  An automation browser may also fail to decode a valid video while firing **no** `error` at all —
  `readyState` stays 0 and only a timeout notices, so an `onError` fallback is structurally dead there;
  `<video>` candidates therefore go **mp4 before webm**, and `canPlayType` is no switch (a measured
  WebKit build answered `"probably"` for the invented codec `vp99`; `skill:verify`, Gotchas).
- Accessibility is a gate: WCAG AA, keyboard nav, screen-reader labels, `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## The round-trip never defers with the browser

- "Browser-verify deferred" defers **only the visual** surface — and only with a named owner and date
  (`30-quality.md`, ADR-0022). The **data** round-trip is browser-free (no session, no auth, no window
  management), so no browser blocker can excuse it: a schema/serialization change always has one, and
  a golden test is required.
- The pattern is **build → serialize → validate → read** — the save schema parses the **serialized**
  form, not the in-memory object; that ordering is what the shipped HTTP 400 hung on — and the test
  asserts the value at stake next to `success` (a schema that also declares the OLD field name parses
  `success: true` while the new one stays `undefined`) and must be RED-verified against the old
  implementation (`30-quality.md`). Canonical snippet, RED-verify duty and rationale live in ONE place:
  `skill:contract-golden-test`. Do not restate the code here.
